curation.lead:
The Humpty Dumpty Institute (HDI, EIN 13-4028567) is a New York-based nonprofit that organized Congressional Delegations (CODELs) to foreign countries, providing all-expenses-paid first-class travel for members of Congress and their staff. The organization is significant to this investigation because Jeffrey Epstein’s brother Mark Epstein served on its board and personally participated in CODELs to Bahrain (2013) and Azerbaijan (2014). Documents recovered from Epstein’s files show that when delegation slots opened, Mark forwarded the opportunities directly to Jeffrey, effectively giving him access to fill Congressional delegation seats with individuals from “media, finance, banking, education” (Finding #1187).

HDI organized more than 52 CODELs involving 550+ members of Congress and staffers to over 30 countries, and maintained an advisory board that included 33 current or former members of Congress, among them Maxine Waters, Jim Clyburn, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, and Gregory Meeks (Finding #1150). Beginning in 2017, HDI entered a formal partnership with China’s Taihe Institute, an organization employing 12 or more current and former members of the Chinese Communist Party and People’s Liberation Army as senior fellows. Despite these foreign government connections, neither HDI nor Taihe registered under the Foreign Agents Registration Act, even as comparable organizations such as the China-United States Exchange Foundation maintained four separate FARA registrations for similar China-US influence activities (Finding #1150).

IRS 990 filings reveal a severe financial contraction: HDI’s revenue peaked at .82 million in 2011 and declined more than 80% to under ,000 per year by 2018, with assets remaining minimal throughout (Finding #426, #460). The organizational contact on IRS records is Ralph Cwerman. Key unresolved questions include whether HDI’s Taihe partnership constitutes acting as an agent of a foreign principal under 22 USC 611(c), what funding sources drove the partial revenue recovery in 2022–2023, and whether Jeffrey Epstein ever successfully placed individuals on Congressional delegations through this channel.

sections.title: The CODEL Pipeline
sections.content:
The core investigative significance of HDI lies in its Congressional Delegation program. The organization facilitated all-expenses-paid, first-class international trips for sitting members of Congress and their staff, organizing more than 52 delegations to over 30 countries including Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Turkey, Cyprus, and events at the United Nations. These delegations provided direct access to foreign heads of state and senior government officials. The Azerbaijan CODEL of May 30 to June 4, 2014, for instance, included meetings with President Ilham Aliyev, US Ambassador Richard Morningstar, and Foreign Affairs Minister Elmar Mammadyarov (Finding #1187).

Mark Epstein, Jeffrey Epstein’s brother and an HDI board member, participated personally in at least two of these delegations. In a December 22, 2014 email recovered as EFTA02598877, Mark wrote to Jeffrey: “We (Humpty Dumpty Institute) led a congressional delegation to Bahrain to meet with ministers and the president (king/head poobah), opposition leaders, senate, head of the US Navy 5th fleet (headquartered in Bahrain) etc. I did not know you were doing this kind of stuff.” This email reveals that Mark was only discovering the overlap between HDI’s activities and Jeffrey’s own geopolitical interests in late 2014.

The mechanism by which Jeffrey Epstein could exploit this pipeline is documented in EFTA02725237. When members dropped out of the Azerbaijan delegation, HDI executive Timothy Merante sought replacements from “media, finance, banking, education.” Mark forwarded this request directly to Jeffrey on May 22, 2014, giving him the opportunity to nominate individuals for Congressional delegation slots. Whether Jeffrey actually placed anyone through this channel remains an open investigative question, but the pipeline—board access, dropout replacement requests, and direct communication to Jeffrey—was clearly operational (Finding #1187).

sections.title: Taihe Institute Partnership and FARA Questions
sections.content:
In 2017, HDI entered a formal partnership with the Taihe Institute, a Beijing-based think tank whose senior fellows include 12 or more current and former members of the Chinese Communist Party and People’s Liberation Army. HDI participated in Taihe forums in Beijing in 2017 and 2019, and the two organizations co-authored publications, including a report that characterized the United States as a “failed country” and advanced the claim that COVID-19 leaked from a Maryland military base (Finding #1150).

Neither HDI nor the Taihe Institute has registered under the Foreign Agents Registration Act. This absence is notable given that China currently has 276 FARA-registered foreign principals, and that the China-United States Exchange Foundation—an organization performing similar China-US influence and exchange activities—maintained four separate FARA registrations through Capitol Counsel (#6328), Wilson Global (#6584), BLJ Worldwide (#5875), and BGR Government Affairs (#5430). HDI has stated that it “never accepted any funds from the Taihe Institute or any Chinese Government organ or entity,” but the legal question is whether the partnership itself constitutes acting as an agent of a foreign principal under 22 USC 611(c), regardless of direct funding (Finding #1150, #388).

The combination of the Taihe partnership with HDI’s existing CODEL infrastructure created a channel through which a CCP-linked institution had a cooperative relationship with an organization that regularly placed members of Congress on international trips and maintained 33 current or former Congress members on its advisory board. This nexus of foreign state ties, Congressional access, and Epstein family involvement, all operating without FARA or Lobbying Disclosure Act registration, represents precisely the kind of regulatory gap that influence operations exploit.

sections.title: Financial Trajectory
sections.content:
IRS 990 filings for HDI (EIN 13-4028567) document a dramatic financial contraction over the 2011–2023 period. Revenue peaked at .82 million in 2011 and began an immediate decline: .64 million in 2012, .70 million in 2013, then accelerating downward to .47 million in 2015, and collapsing to approximately ,000 by 2016. By 2018, annual revenue had fallen below ,000, representing an 80% decline from the 2011 peak. Total assets, which reached ,000 at their height in 2011, remained minimal throughout, hovering around ,000 in recent years (Finding #426, #460).

The financial trajectory shows HDI consistently spent more than it earned but survived by operating on razor-thin margins with minimal reserves. A partial revenue recovery appeared in 2022–2023, with revenue reaching approximately ,000 and ,000 respectively. This late-period uptick may reflect new funding sources unrelated to the Epstein network, though the specific donors have not been identified from available 990 data. The organizational contact listed on IRS records throughout this period is Ralph Cwerman, who serves as the institutional point person for the entity.

The scale of HDI’s contraction mirrors a pattern observed in the International Peace Institute, another nonprofit in the Epstein orbit that experienced significant financial decline, though HDI operated at a much smaller scale throughout. The timing of the revenue collapse—beginning immediately after the 2011 peak and accelerating through the mid-2010s—warrants investigation into whether it correlates with changes in donor relationships, the increasing public scrutiny of Epstein-adjacent organizations, or shifts in HDI’s CODEL activity levels.

open_questions: Did Jeffrey Epstein ever successfully place individuals on HDI Congressional delegations after Mark forwarded the Azerbaijan vacancy request in May 2014?
Does HDI's Taihe Institute partnership constitute acting as an agent of a foreign principal under 22 USC 611(c), even absent direct Chinese government funding?
What specific funding sources drove HDI's partial revenue recovery in 2022-2023, and are any connected to the Taihe partnership or other foreign entities?
Who is Ruby Wang, identified as bridging both HDI and Taihe Institute, and what role did she play in establishing the 2017 partnership?
What was the full scope of Mark Epstein's involvement with HDI beyond the Bahrain and Azerbaijan CODELs -- did he participate in the planned Turkey/Cyprus delegation mentioned in EFTA02598877?
